mutants.name: ntt-wrong-zeta
mutants.description: src/mlkem_tables.inc: zetas[77] := zetas[76] (both planes). One entry, block 13 of the last NTT layer.

mutants.name: reduce-bound-off-by-one
mutants.description: mlkem_poly_reduce gets a private conditional subtract whose threshold is q instead of q-1, so v == k*q comes back as q. (The shared CSUBQ also feeds arith_init/add/basemul, so the fault is scoped to reduce; +258 B pad keeps RODATA's page offset.)

mutants.name: ntt-missing-final-reduce
mutants.description: REPLACED: this implementation canonicalises inside every butterfly and has no final pass. Nearest fault of the class: the high-byte half of the masked subtract on f[X]+t is dropped (`sbc fq_e_lo` -> `sbc #0`), so sums >= q leave the layer non-canonical.

mutants.name: butterfly-swapped-operand
mutants.description: NTT butterfly computes f[Y] = t - f[X] instead of f[X] - t (operands of the subtract exchanged; same size).

mutants.name: loop-bpl-256
mutants.description: mlkem_poly_add counts X down from 255 with dex/bpl: bit 7 of 254 is set, so the loop runs exactly once (P1's keccak_clear shape).
mutants.expect: mlkem_poly_add[all q-1, all q-1]: first diff at coeff 0

mutants.name: basemul-accumulator-24bit
mutants.description: REPLACED: every product is reduced before it is combined, so no 24-bit accumulator exists. Nearest fault of the class 'operand exceeds the multiply's width assumption': the (x0+x1) sum feeding the Karatsuba middle product is not reduced (jsr fq_csubq_p -> 3 nops), so a1 reaches 26 and the 14x14 |d| table is over-run.
mutants.expect: mlkem_poly_basemul[all q-1 x all q-1  (S4 accumulator width)]

mutants.name: basemul-zeta-sign
mutants.description: The parity test `and #2` becomes `and #0`: every pair takes the even (+gamma) path; the odd pairs no longer subtract.

mutants.name: sub-no-wrap

mutants.name: intt-scale-wrong

mutants.name: ntt-data-dependent-branch
mutants.description: The masked conditional subtract on f[X]+t in the NTT butterfly becomes a `bcc`-guarded store: functionally identical, one cycle per butterfly depends on the coefficient. Same size (29 B + nop).

mutants.name: ntt-a1-range-12
mutants.description: EXTRA: the block table U[k] stops at k = 12 (`cpx #14` -> `cpx #13`), restoring the a1 <= 12 assumption; a = q-1 = $0D00 is the only coefficient that reaches U[13].

mutants.name: wp3-cmp-mismatch-timing
mutants.description: EXTRA (hardware-validation adversary, `ct-leak3`): cmp_len still OR-accumulates every byte of the full 1,088 B (functionally correct, no early exit), but a mismatching byte takes a different path (`beq same` / `sta cmp_acc` / `bne next`) that costs one more cycle than a matching one (two as linked: `bne next` also crosses a page): decaps time leaks the NUMBER of differing bytes. The equal-byte path is cycle-identical to the original ora+sta, so a valid c measures exactly the green count; a 6 B lead-in plus a 246 B pad make the patch +256 B, so every later byte keeps its page offset. Under `make test` check-manifest also fails, because the pad puts resident bytes above the declared 7,424.

mutants.name: p1-keccak-rc23-bit0
mutants.description: P1 (hardware-validation adversary, `k-rc23`): src/keccak_tables.inc, the round-23 iota constant's low byte $08 -> $09 (one bit of the last round constant; the generated table patched as if hand-edited). Rounds 0-22 and every other step are exact.

mutants.name: p1-sponge-len-hi-ignored
mutants.description: P1 (hardware-validation adversary, `k-chunk-hi`): the sponge chunk size ignores the high byte of the remaining length (`bne done` -> 2 nop). Any len >= 256 is worn down to a nonzero multiple of 256, where the chunk is n = 0 and absorb never advances: a LIVELOCK. The kill is the harness's 5 s jsr timeout on mlkem_absorb (expect pins that traceback frame, so a timeout at any other call site is a non-local kill) (VICE is torn down by the suite's ViceInstanceManager); mutate.py has no timeout of its own.
